tier_reason: The well-known independent lzbench 2.4 suite (public code, inikep/lzbench; gcc 15.2.0 release binary; single thread of an AMD EPYC 9555P, turbo off, silesia.tar) lists density 0.16.6 -1 at 1630 / 1617 MB/s, 62.77% vs lz4 1.10.0 --fast -17 at 924 / 3977 MB/s, 62.15% and lz4 1.10.0 at 550 / 3832 MB/s, 47.60%; all quoted rows match. Density is built through cargo --release inside lzbench and the release binary's exact build settings are not on the results page, so B rather than A, consistent with other lzbench-sourced entries.
notes: All numbers verified on the lzbench README; last commit 2025-08-27 (stale, 13 months), MIT/Apache-2.0, about 1k stars. Implementation language is Rust, so the orchestrator may want to tag it as a non-C++ entry; the README itself has no numeric comparison against lz4/snappy (it only claims pareto-frontier and points to cargo bench).

tier_reason: The independent lzbench 2.4 suite (public code, gcc 15.2.0 release binary, single thread of an AMD EPYC 9555P, silesia.tar) lists bsc 3.3.12 -m0 -e1 at 19.4 / 25.0 MB/s, 23.26% vs xz 5.8.4 -5 at 3.84 / 121 MB/s, 23.70% and xz -9 at 2.75 / 122 MB/s, 23.01%; all quoted rows match. Release-binary build details (notably OpenMP) are not on the results page, so B.

corrections.caveats: Decompression is much slower than xz in the same table (25.0 MB/s versus about 121 MB/s). The libbsc README has no benchmark numbers, so all evidence comes from the lzbench table. lzbench notes bsc multithreaded decompress faults on 32-bit ARM. The lzbench Makefile compiles bsc with OpenMP multithreading when OpenMP is found, and the results page does not say whether the release binary used it, so the single-thread claim for bsc is not certain.

notes: Numbers verified; Apache-2.0, 352 stars, last commit 2026-02-03 (active). Added the OpenMP build caveat from the lzbench Makefile.

tier_reason: The independent lzbench 2.4 suite (public code, gcc 15.2.0 release binary, single thread of an AMD EPYC 9555P, silesia.tar) lists zling 2018-10-12 -0 at 86.1 / 183 MB/s, 29.72% vs zlib 1.3.2 -6 at 26.8 / 314 MB/s, 32.19%; the README separately shows libzling e0 2.208 s vs gzip 6.502 s on enwik8 (Xeon E5-2620 v3). All quoted numbers match; flags of the release binary are not on the results page, so B.
notes: Numbers verified on both pages; archived 2021-04-26, last commit 2018-10-12 (abandoned), BSD-3-Clause text in source headers with no LICENSE file (confirmed LICENSE/LICENSE.txt/COPYING 404). lzbench marks zling as not recommended for production use (per author).
